subject: Proof of Erasure & Data Handback: SOC 2 artifact questions
messages:
From: Nathan Cole <nathan.cole@calyxbank.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Cc: audits@clearcompliance.io
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: SOC 2 evidence for tenant erasure and data handback

Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As part of our SOC 2 readiness review, our external auditors (audits@clearcompliance.io) have asked for artifacts that demonstrate the lifecycle for tenant data deletion and the ability to hand back/transfer residual data when requested. Specifically they want:

- A sample export that shows mapping from customer tenant IDs to physical shard/region (for proof of residency).
- A sample erasure log for a tenant deletion (including timestamps and job ids).
- Confirmation of TTL settings in our DB/config and a screenshot or config dump showing the TTL policy applied.

Can you point me to the right artifacts and a short narrative (3–4 bullets) we can hand to auditors explaining the orchestration flow (who triggers deletion, propagation windows, verification & retention of deletion logs)? We have a target to include this in our auditor packet by EOD Thursday 18 Jun.

Let me know if you need a longer window.

Best,
Nathan
Nathan Cole
Infrastructure Security Lead, Calyx Bank
From: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai <lukas_meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Nathan Cole <nathan.cole@calyxbank.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 evidence for tenant erasure and data handback

Hi Nathan — thanks for the clear list. We can produce all three artifact types. Quick plan:

1) Tenant mapping: export (CSV) showing tenant_id, region, cluster_id — includes last_active_at and owner tag.
2) Erasure log: we will extract a redacted sample showing deletion job id, started_at, completed_at, files deleted count, and verification checksum.
3) TTL/config confirmation: screenshot of DB TTL config plus the infra-as-code snippet that sets TTL; we will redact any internal IPs.

Irene, Karthik — can you prepare the three artifacts and a 3-bullet narrative that explains the workflow and SLOs for deletion verification? We need these packaged and uploaded to the Drive link below by EOD Thu 18 Jun to meet Calyx's audit window.

Drive folder (will upload): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleProof

Nathan — a couple clarifications we may include in the narrative: deletion propagation window (typically up to 2 hours for metadata, up to 24 hours for cold-tier cleanup), whether we maintain any hashed snapshots solely for debugging (we keep rolling, encrypted logs for 30 days), and an attestation line re: no backup copies retained beyond retention windows.

Irene / Karthik — please confirm ETA.

Thanks,
Lukas
Lukas Meyer
Manager, Platform Security Operations
Redwood Inference
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:23:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Request: SOC 2 evidence for tenant erasure and data handback

Forwarding Nathan's auditor ask and Lukas' plan. I pulled sample artifacts and attached them here for review before upload. The attachments are redacted for tenant identifiers but retain the schema & audit fields auditors require.

Attachments:
- calyx_tenant_map.csv (columns: tenant_id_redacted, region, cluster_id, owner_tag, last_active_at)
- erasure-sample-log.txt (deletion_job: dj-1782, started_at: 2026-05-11T21:02:11Z, completed_at: 2026-05-11T21:05:43Z, deleted_objects: 124, verification_checksum: sha256:abcd...)
- db-ttl-config-screenshot.png (console shot of TTL config + IaC snippet as comment)

Draft narrative for auditors (please keep short):
- Deletion orchestration: Deletion requests (tenant-initiated or admin) create a deletion job that marks tenant as DELETING and enqueues metadata & object cleanup workers. Metadata removal is executed first (SLO: <2 hours) followed by object lifecycle purge across cold vs hot storage (SLO: <24 hours).
- Verification & logging: Each deletion job writes a signed erasure log record on completion; logs persisted to an immutable logs bucket for 30 days for auditability and to support replay if required.
- Handback/export: Tenant mapping exports are generated on demand; we provide a CSV mapping tenant identifiers to physical clusters and regions. Exports are redacted and delivered over a secure share; we do not keep long-term copies after delivery unless contractually required.

Vanessa — can you validate the attached samples meet auditor expectations and upload to the Drive folder. Also confirm whether a DocuSign attestation is needed or if I can provide a signed email from Lukas.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Nathan Cole <nathan.cole@calyxbank.com>
Cc: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:01:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 evidence for tenant erasure and data handback

Hi Nathan — uploaded the redacted artifacts to the Drive folder and included a one-page cover note and the short narrative (both in the folder). Items uploaded: calyx_tenant_map.csv, erasure-sample-log.txt, db-ttl-config-screenshot.png, and attestation-email.pdf (signed export of Lukas' confirmation).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleProof
DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/EXAMPLE-12345 (attestation prepared; let us know if you prefer a DocuSign signature flow)

A couple of practical notes for auditors:
- The erasure log sample is unredacted for job ids and timestamps but tenant ids are hashed for customer privacy. Full tenant ids can be provided under NDA or a scoped request.
- TTL policies are enforced via IaC; screenshot includes the IaC comment block referencing ttl_days per bucket.

If auditors need anything else (additional samples, longer retention of the artifacts while they review), tell us the exact scope and retention SLA and we'll accommodate.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
